project.name: Computer Use Workbench
project.description: A local single-user workbench for running provider-native Computer Use agents, managing their sessions, workflows, credentials, and execution records.

nodes.name: Computer Use Session Execution
nodes.summary: This domain creates and controls Computer Use sessions for user-supplied tasks. It bridges typed session requests to the existing execution engine and retains session state for subsequent access.

businessRules: A requested model must be present in the catalog before a session is created.
Session stop and deletion operations stop orchestration before removing a stored session.
crossDomainInteractions: Uses provider models, routes, and credential sessions to start execution.
Produces session records consumed by audit and analytics.

nodes.name: Provider Configuration
nodes.summary: This domain exposes the validated Computer Use model catalog and available provider routes. It also manages process-local credential sessions so provider secrets are not persisted or serialized.

businessRules: Credential sessions have a bounded lifetime of at most eight hours.
Credential secrets are never persisted or serialized.
crossDomainInteractions: Supplies selectable models, routes, and credentials to session execution.

nodes.name: Workflow Authoring
nodes.summary: This domain lets an operator define declarative workflows, record their versions, and compile them. Workflow data is represented in the v2 API and persisted alongside other v2 records.

businessRules: A workflow must exist before it can be versioned or compiled.
crossDomainInteractions: Uses the shared v2 persistence store that also records session data.

nodes.name: Execution Audit and Analytics
nodes.summary: This domain makes persisted session actions, events, metrics, and aggregate analytics available to operators. Its records support inspection of Computer Use execution after or while sessions run.

businessRules: Session action, event, and metric collections are paginated.
Analytics can be filtered by session, model, or route.
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes records produced by Computer Use session execution.

nodes.name: Sandbox and Reference Inputs
nodes.summary: This domain operates the Docker-hosted Computer Use environment and accepts reference files for runs. It exposes environment status and lifecycle controls alongside server-side file storage endpoints.

businessRules: Reference-file support differs by provider; Gemini Computer Use rejects these files.
crossDomainInteractions: Provides the runtime environment and reference inputs used by Computer Use sessions.

nodes.name: Create Computer Use Session
nodes.summary: Creates a typed v2 session for a requested Computer Use task and starts its execution path.

nodes.name: Control Computer Use Session
nodes.summary: Stops or deletes an existing v2 session through its session resource endpoints.

nodes.name: Discover Provider Routes
nodes.summary: Returns cataloged Computer Use models and the provider routes available for them.

nodes.name: Manage Credential Session
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary credential session and allows the caller to remove it when it is no longer needed.

nodes.name: Create Workflow
nodes.summary: Stores a workflow definition containing its slug, name, variables schema, and steps.

nodes.name: Version Workflow
nodes.summary: Adds a new version to an existing workflow and returns the resulting workflow representation.

nodes.name: Compile Workflow
nodes.summary: Loads an existing workflow and compiles it using the supplied compile input.

nodes.name: Review Session Audit
nodes.summary: Retrieves paginated actions, events, and metrics recorded for a session.

nodes.name: Analyze Execution Data
nodes.summary: Returns aggregate execution analytics, optionally narrowed to a session, model, or route.

nodes.name: Manage Sandbox Container
nodes.summary: Reports, builds, starts, and stops the Docker container that hosts the Computer Use environment.

nodes.name: Manage Reference Files
nodes.summary: Accepts a file into server-side storage and lets the caller remove a previously uploaded file.

nodes.name: Validate Requested Model
nodes.summary: Looks up the requested model in the catalog and returns an error when it is invalid.

nodes.name: Create Session
nodes.summary: Handles the typed session-creation request at the v2 sessions endpoint.

nodes.name: Bridge Session to Execution
nodes.summary: Passes v2 session execution through the orchestrator bridge to the existing Computer Use engine.

nodes.name: Load Session
nodes.summary: Retrieves the stored session addressed by the requested session identifier.

nodes.name: Stop Orchestration
nodes.summary: Stops the session through the v2 orchestrator before its state is changed or removed.

nodes.name: Delete Stored Session
nodes.summary: Deletes the session from the persistence store and returns not found when it is absent.

nodes.name: List Catalog Models
nodes.summary: Returns model payloads with the catalog version and verification timestamp.

nodes.name: Iterate Model Routes
nodes.summary: Walks catalog models to assemble the provider-route response data.

nodes.name: Deduplicate Routes
nodes.summary: Uses a seen set while building the provider-route response.

nodes.name: Create Vault Session
nodes.summary: Creates a credential session in the process-local credential vault.

nodes.name: Validate Credential Input
nodes.summary: Converts vault validation failures into the credential-session API response.

nodes.name: Delete Vault Session
nodes.summary: Removes a credential session from the credential vault by identifier.

nodes.name: Accept Workflow Input
nodes.summary: Accepts the typed workflow input at the workflow creation endpoint.

nodes.name: Persist Workflow
nodes.summary: Creates the workflow using its slug, name, variables schema, and steps.

nodes.name: Return Workflow Payload
nodes.summary: Serializes the created workflow for the API response.

nodes.name: Accept Version Input
nodes.summary: Receives a typed version request for the addressed workflow.

nodes.name: Create Workflow Version
nodes.summary: Creates a new workflow version through the persistence store.

nodes.name: Report Version Error
nodes.summary: Returns an API error response when workflow version creation fails validation.

nodes.name: Load Workflow for Compilation
nodes.summary: Retrieves the addressed workflow before compilation.

nodes.name: Reject Missing Workflow
nodes.summary: Returns a not-found error when the workflow requested for compilation is absent.

nodes.name: Compile Workflow Definition
nodes.summary: Compiles the existing workflow using the supplied workflow compile input.

nodes.name: List Session Actions
nodes.summary: Returns a paginated collection of actions for a session.

nodes.name: List Session Events
nodes.summary: Returns a paginated collection of events for a session.

nodes.name: List Session Metrics
nodes.summary: Returns a paginated collection of metrics for a session.

nodes.name: Accept Analytics Filters
nodes.summary: Accepts optional session, model, and route filters for analytics.

nodes.name: Query Analytics
nodes.summary: Delegates aggregate analytics retrieval to the v2 persistence store.

nodes.name: Report Container Status
nodes.summary: Returns Docker container and agent-service status.

nodes.name: Start Container
nodes.summary: Builds if needed and starts the Computer Use Docker container.

nodes.name: Stop Container
nodes.summary: Stops running agents and removes the Docker container.

nodes.name: Accept File Upload
nodes.summary: Persists a single uploaded file into the server-side store.

nodes.name: Store Reference File
nodes.summary: Uses provider-aware reference-file handling for Computer Use runs.

nodes.name: Delete Uploaded File
nodes.summary: Removes a previously uploaded file from storage and disk.

edges.description: Session creation depends on cataloged models, provider routes, and temporary credentials.
Audit and analytics queries consume records for Computer Use sessions.
The sandbox and reference-file capabilities support Computer Use runs.
Workflow and execution audit data share the v2 persistence layer.
